prompt: You have 15 coins, all nickels and dimes, worth $\$1.10$ total. How many nickels do you have?
hint: Two rules in cents: $n + d = 15$ coins and $5n + 10d = 110$ cents.

hints.text: Two rules in cents: $n + d = 15$ coins and $5n + 10d = 110$ cents.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try all-nickels first: $15$ nickels is only $\$0.75$ — too little by $\$0.35$. Every dime swap adds $\$0.05$, so count the swaps.

explanation: Count rule: $n + d = 15$. Money rule in cents: $5n + 10d = 110$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pretend they are all dimes
steps: If all 15 coins were dimes, you would have 150 cents — that is 40 cents too much.
Swapping a dime for a nickel drops the total by 5 cents. You need 40 ÷ 5 = 8 swaps, so 8 nickels.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: 10 nickels, 5 dimes: 50 + 50 = 100 cents. Too low. 6 nickels, 9 dimes: 30 + 90 = 120. Too high.
8 nickels, 7 dimes: 40 + 70 = 110 cents. That is the match — 8 nickels.
